text: 我不支持卖淫合法，但我觉得大势所趋，阻止不了。
en: I do not support legalising prostitution, but I think it is the inevitable trend of the times and cannot be stopped.

text: 一二三产业，女性也就能在第三产业里跟男性勉强五五开。
en: In the primary, secondary and tertiary industries, women can only just about hold their own against men in the tertiary sector, roughly fifty-fifty.

text: 现在经济下行，第三产业更冷。
en: With the economy now in decline, the tertiary sector is even more depressed.

text: 女性怎么办？
en: What are women to do?

text: 要么走出去，去本就很卷很苦逼的一二产业跟男性竞争。
en: Either go out and compete with men in the already brutally cut-throat and miserable primary and secondary industries.

text: 要么躺下去，凭借大自然的底层设计创造新的就业。
en: Or lie down and create new employment by relying on nature's underlying design.

text: 要么滚回去，经营家庭（当然这是当前女性非常反感的）。
en: Or go back and run the household (though of course this is something women today deeply resent).

text: 就这么简单、残酷，没有丝毫温情。
en: It is that simple and that brutal, with not a shred of warmth.

text: 来逐条回应一下对话里的漏洞。
en: Let me respond point by point to the flaws in the discussion.

text: 1. “卖淫合法了，会使强奸犯变少。
en: 1. "If prostitution is legalised, there would be fewer rapists.

text: 假设错。
en: The premise is wrong.

text: 强奸不是“没地儿发泄”，而是权力犯罪：支配、羞辱、报复、控制，甚至是把对方的恐惧当成战利品。
en: Rape is not "having no outlet for release"; it is a crime of power: domination, humiliation, revenge, control, even treating the other person's fear as a trophy.

text: 如果只是生理需求，强奸犯早就可以去买现成的性服务；大量熟人强奸、伴侣强奸也解释不了。
en: If it were merely a physiological need, rapists could long ago have gone and bought ready-made sexual services; the large number of acquaintance rapes and partner rapes cannot be explained by that either.

text: 所以合法化→强奸减少的逻辑链条不成立。
en: Therefore the logical chain that legalisation leads to fewer rapes does not hold.

text: 2. “合法后，自愿卖淫竞争上岗，不漂亮的还没人要。
en: 2. "After legalisation, voluntary prostitutes compete for posts, and the less attractive ones won't even be wanted.

text: 这句话之所以让人愤怒，是因为它把性产业想成普通就业，把女性想成市场里的“供给单位”。
en: The reason this remark enrages people is that it imagines the sex industry as ordinary employment and women as "units of supply" in the market.

text: 但性产业不是简历投递，它叠着贫穷、债务、家暴、未成年、性别不平等，是一个结构性高风险行业。
en: But the sex industry is not a matter of submitting CVs; it is layered with poverty, debt, domestic violence, minors and gender inequality, and is a structurally high-risk industry.

text: 现实经验告诉我们：合法行业和黑市往往并存，合法区可能反而在后门就是黑市。
en: Experience tells us: the legal industry and the black market often coexist, and the legal zone may in fact have the black market right at its back door.

text: 对方在谈“男人有没有选择”，但这个行业的真问题是“女人（承认大多数从业者还是女性）有没有退路”。
en: The other side talks about "whether men have a choice", but the real question for this industry is "whether women (admitting that most workers are still women) have a way out".

text: 3. “拿牌营业，就不存在逼迫。
en: 3. "Once you operate with a licence, there is no coercion.

text: 如果牌照能消灭暴力，那家暴、拐卖、地下色情早就不存在了。
en: If licences could eliminate violence, then domestic violence, trafficking and underground pornography would have vanished long ago.

text: 暴力不会因为你允许就消失，只会因为监管变强而收缩。
en: Violence does not disappear just because you permit it; it only shrinks when regulation is strengthened.

text: 合法化想真正起作用，需要一整套制度协同：警力、执法预算、健康检查、行业监察、社会保障、反拐卖机制…
en: For legalisation to truly work, it requires a whole set of institutional coordination: police capacity, law-enforcement budgets, health checks, industry oversight, social security, anti-trafficking mechanisms…

text: 任何一个环节薄弱，黑市和逼迫都会回潮。
en: If any single link is weak, the black market and coercion will resurge.

text: 市场不是万能药。
en: The market is not a panacea.

text: 4. “你这么反感，不会是你对象嫖过吧。
en: 4. "You react so strongly — surely your partner hasn't paid for sex?

text: 这是把讨论从公共问题拉回私事，典型的转移话题。
en: This drags the discussion back from a public issue to a private matter — a classic change of subject.

text: 5. 至于你那句：“不嫖娼会死吗？
en: 5. As for that line of yours: "Will you die if you don't pay for sex?

text: 被激怒很正常。
en: It is perfectly normal to be enraged.

text: 因为对方整套逻辑把女性降格成满足需求的工具，把男性欲望当成公共政策的中心。
en: Because the other side's entire logic demotes women to tools for satisfying needs and treats male desire as the centre of public policy.

text: 但真正要抓住的问题不是“你支持还是反对合法化”，而是：用什么逻辑，为了保护谁。
en: But the real question to grasp is not "do you support or oppose legalisation", but: by what logic, and to protect whom.

text: 说下我的看法。
en: Let me set out my own view.

text: 说实话，我不想把卖淫合法化当洪水猛兽。
en: To be honest, I do not want to treat the legalisation of prostitution as some great scourge.

text: 我反感的是很多人在讨论它时既天真又目中无人，一边假装理性，一边只考虑男人的便利。
en: What I resent is that many people, when discussing it, are both naive and self-important, pretending to be rational on the one hand while only considering men's convenience on the other.

text: 有时候我觉得，在天朝谈合法化，像在一间灯光忽明忽暗的屋子里，大家举着手电筒互晃脸，却没人照到真正黑的地方。
en: Sometimes I feel that discussing legalisation in Tianchao is like being in a room with flickering lights, where everyone raises a torch and shines it at each other's faces, yet no one illuminates the truly dark corners.

text: 支持者轻飘飘地谈供需、自由、市场，仿佛“合法”两个字落地，逼迫就会自动消失；
en: Supporters talk airily about supply and demand, freedom and the market, as if the two characters "legal" merely landing on the ground would make coercion vanish automatically;

text: 反对者则立刻联想到道德崩塌、社会沦陷，仿佛讨论本身就是大忌。
en: Opponents, for their part, immediately conjure up moral collapse and social downfall, as if merely discussing it were a grave taboo.

text: 可两边经常忘了，“卖淫”不是一个政策名词，而是一群正在被制度推搡的人。
en: Yet both sides often forget that "prostitution" is not a policy term, but a group of people being shoved around by the system.

text: 她们可能是为房租、孩子学费、家里债务被挤进来的女人；
en: They may be women pushed into it by rent, their children's school fees and household debt;

text: 可能是十五六岁就被带去小旅馆、被拍照控制的女孩；
en: They may be girls taken to small hotels at fifteen or sixteen and controlled through photographs;

text: 也可能是躲在阴影里互相递TT、提醒彼此别出事的人。
en: They may also be people hiding in the shadows, passing each other condoms and warning one another to stay safe.

text: 她们活在现实里，不活在我们的道德口号或市场想象里。
en: They live in reality, not in our moral slogans or market imaginings.

text: 所以我不接受那种“合法化能治好强奸”的直觉式雄性理性，也不接受那种“谈合法化就是败德”的文化羞耻。
en: So I do not accept that intuitive, masculine "legalisation can cure rape" rationality, nor do I accept that cultural shame of "discussing legalisation is moral corruption".

text: 真正的问题永远是制度：你是让风险更隐蔽，还是让风险可见、可管、可追责？
en: The real question is always the system: do you make the risk more hidden, or make it visible, manageable and accountable?

text: 合法化不是答案，只是工具。
en: Legalisation is not the answer; it is only a tool.

text: 工具好不好，取决于你用它保护谁。
en: Whether a tool is good or not depends on whom you use it to protect.

text: 有的国家合法化后街区更安全，不是因为世界变纯洁了，而是因为警察敢进、执法可监测、健康检查透明、暴力有渠道举报、未成年人更容易被识别。
en: In some countries, after legalisation the neighbourhoods became safer, not because the world grew pure, but because the police dared to enter, enforcement became monitorable, health checks became transparent, there were channels to report violence, and minors became easier to identify.

text: 那些原本在黑暗里的人，至少被看见了。
en: Those who were originally in the dark at least became visible.

text: 我们争的不应该是“卖淫是不是可以”，而是一个社会愿不愿意承认它存在，并用法治把伤害压到最低。
en: What we should be arguing over is not "whether prostitution is acceptable", but whether a society is willing to acknowledge its existence and use the rule of law to minimise the harm.

text: 如果讨论卖淫合法化时，你只关心男人有没有地方排泄，那你没资格谈制度；
en: If, when discussing the legalisation of prostitution, you only care whether men have somewhere to relieve themselves, then you are in no position to talk about the system;

text: 如果你因为害怕道德混乱就拒绝一切治理工具，你也同样没在谈制度。
en: If you reject all tools of governance out of fear of moral chaos, then you too are not really talking about the system.

text: 成熟的讨论必须同时承认三件事：
en: A mature discussion must acknowledge three things at once:

text: 卖淫存在，风险存在，人的处境也存在。
en: Prostitution exists, risk exists, and people's predicament exists too.

text: 看见这三件事，才配开始讨论该怎么管。
en: Only by seeing these three things does one earn the right to begin discussing how to regulate it.

text: 卖淫，自古以来都有啊！
en: Prostitution has existed since ancient times!

text: 合不合法能阻止么？
en: Can legal or illegal stop it?

text: 道德上将被包养，短期女友，三十万彩礼都算卖淫，
en: Morally speaking, being kept, being a short-term girlfriend, and a three-hundred-thousand-yuan bride price all count as prostitution,

text: 法律上是以盈利为目的性行为，包括边缘性行为。
en: Legally it is sexual conduct for the purpose of profit, including borderline sexual acts.

text: 伟人用了一辈子将这片土地上的大烟馆，妓院给关了，等他死后两年，改革开放后立马又被一批人捡起来了。
en: The great man spent his whole life shutting down the opium dens and brothels across this land; just two years after his death, once reform and opening up began, a group of people promptly picked them up again.

text: 这他妈才是中国女人地位降低的开始！
en: This, damn it, is the true beginning of the decline in the status of Chinese women!

text: 尊重女人是把她当个公主一样捧起来么？
en: Is respecting women a matter of lifting her up like a princess?

text: 是让她跟个宠物一样只负责卖萌受宠么？
en: Is it letting her, like a pet, be responsible only for acting cute and being doted on?

text: 我觉得中国女人权利的巅峰是全民皆兵时期，三十左右的妇女，养活着四五个孩子，下了地，参加民兵集训，56 式分解结合，立跪卧枪枪上靶，木柄手榴弹原地撇三四十米，换到现在很多作战单位士兵都达不到。
en: I think the peak of Chinese women's rights was the period of total militarisation, when women around thirty were raising four or five children, working the fields, attending militia training, performing Type 56 disassembly and reassembly, and hitting the target from standing, kneeling and prone positions; hurling wooden-handled grenades thirty or forty metres on the spot — feats that, today, many combat-unit soldiers could not achieve.

text: 各种会议妇女都有代表参加，这是她们权利的巅峰。
en: Women had representatives attending all kinds of meetings; this was the peak of their rights.

text: 一旦合法化，就意味着伟人一生的努力付诸东流，就意味着好不容易站起来的妇女精神沦落为一句空话，妇女能顶半边天这句话也将不复存在！
en: Once legalised, it would mean the great man's lifelong efforts come to nothing; it would mean the hard-won spirit of women who had only just stood up degenerates into empty words, and the saying "women hold up half the sky" would cease to exist!

text: 我们是社会主义！
en: We are a socialist country!

text: 是一个人人平等，人人有权利的国度。
en: A nation where everyone is equal and everyone has rights.

text: 市场经济是向时代妥协的结果，但是在人权方面，国家绝对不能开这个先口，这是个底线！
en: The market economy is the result of compromise with the times, but on the matter of human rights the state absolutely must not open this precedent — this is a bottom line!

text: 卖淫是这个时代妇女的个体做法，绝对不能上升到国家许可！
en: Prostitution is an individual practice of women in this era and must never be elevated to state sanction!

text: 无论出于什么原因，个人的原委不能上升到国家的路线。
en: Whatever the reason, an individual's circumstances must not be elevated to the level of the state's line.

text: 当然我也挺同情她们的，市场经济下，其实就是物竞天择（资产底蕴也算在个人的能力上），这就导致了很多女人在这场竞争中失利，职场上就是歧视女性。
en: Of course I also rather sympathise with them. Under the market economy, it comes down to survival of the fittest (assets and family backing count as part of personal ability), and this leads many women to lose out in this competition; in the workplace there is simply discrimination against women.

text: 一切能力基于体力精力，体力精力不分家，女人先天的条件不足，这就导致了她们绝大多数竞争不过男性，考学不算全部，具体要看工作能力。
en: All ability is based on physical strength and energy, and the two are inseparable; women's innate conditions are insufficient, which means the vast majority cannot compete with men. Examination results are not the whole story — what matters specifically is work ability.

text: 03 年左右计算机专业兴起，很多人觉得这是专门给女人提供的岗位，轻快自在，结果几年下来，搞计算机的全程男性了，就连裁缝这一类细活，做得好的也多数是男性。
en: Around 2003 the computer science discipline emerged, and many thought it was a job specially provided for women — light and easy — yet a few years on, computing was entirely men, and even in fine work like tailoring, it is mostly men who do it well.

text: 女性还有一大致命缺陷，合作性极差！
en: Women also have one major fatal flaw: extremely poor cooperativeness!

text: 三个米粒沾不到一块，多了不讲懂得都懂，girls help girls 本身就是一场闹剧。
en: Three grains of rice won't stick together; I won't say more, those who understand understand — "girls help girls" is itself a farce.

text: 女性还有一大弱点，情绪不稳定，理性容易被感性压制，导致她们很难胜任领导层，很容易被对位压制。
en: Women also have a major weakness: unstable emotions, with reason easily overpowered by feeling, making it hard for them to be competent in leadership and easily suppressed by their counterparts.

text: 基于这些因素，女性在学校付出比男性更多的精力读书，就业远比男性艰难，更何况学校本身也不想教人什么东西。
en: Because of these factors, women devote more energy than men to studying at school, yet find employment far harder than men, not to mention that schools themselves have no real interest in teaching anything.

text: 很多女性就业后发现，自己拼命读书竟然不如被领导潜一次规则来的钱块，自己以为代表能力的成绩竟然不如倒数的骚浪贱扭扭屁股实用。
en: Many women, after finding employment, discover that their desperate studying earns less than sleeping with the boss once, and that the grades they thought represented ability are less useful than the lowest-ranked flirt wiggling her hips.

text: 众多因素折磨着现代职场女性。
en: Numerous factors torment modern working women.

text: 当然，如果学习真的很牛，可以走科研路线，但是，同样成绩的人，导师优先选择男性，就凭他更能干活。
en: Of course, if one truly excels at studying, one can take the research route; but among people with equal results, the supervisor gives priority to men, simply because they can work harder.

text: 还有消费主义盛行，物欲横流，没钱支付高额消费，这也是大学生卖淫的重要原因，内心空洞，需要物质来满足虚荣心，夹杂现实与幻想之间倍受折磨，一方面成为很多人幻想的对象，一方面有想要不属于自己奢华人生，因此选择卖淫来挣去外快，又造成的内心空洞，恶性循环下去。
en: Then there is the prevalence of consumerism and rampant material desire; lacking the money to pay for high consumption is also a major reason university students turn to prostitution. With an inner emptiness, they need material things to satisfy their vanity, suffering torment caught between reality and fantasy — on the one hand becoming the object of many people's fantasies, on the other wanting a luxurious life that is not their own; thus they choose prostitution to earn extra money, which in turn deepens their inner emptiness, a vicious cycle.

text: 基于以上这些，我不反对那些活不下去的人卖淫，命运很是无常，总是喜欢欺负苦命人，为了活得更好这没错。
en: On the basis of all the above, I do not oppose those who cannot survive turning to prostitution. Fate is fickle and always seems to pick on the wretched; wanting to live better is not wrong.

text: 那些职场女性或许迫于压力，也会向现实妥协，还有那些被填鸭式教育压抑二十多年的女性，以此为排解。
en: Those working women may, under pressure, also compromise with reality; and there are those women repressed for over twenty years by cramming-style education, who use it as a release.

text: 最后还有那些虚荣心爆棚的人，让她卖去吧。
en: Finally there are those bursting with vanity — let them go and sell themselves.

text: 法律摆在那里，路线政策原则不会因为一些人而改变，个人原因在国家面前不值一提，想挣这个钱就去挣，被抓的代价可以接受，内心空洞的因果可要吃一辈子。
en: The law stands there; the principles of the line and policy will not change because of a few individuals. Personal reasons count for nothing before the state. If you want to earn this money, go earn it; if the cost of being caught is acceptable, so be it — but the cause and effect of an inner emptiness you will have to live with for a lifetime.
